question.value: How does the vertical dust scale height differ between inner and outer rings of resolved double-ring protoplanetary disks, measured from azimuthal intensity variations in ALMA Band 6 continuum rings?

evidence.quote: We investigate the vertical dust distribution in 6 protoplanetary disks with resolved double rings, using high-resolution ALMA Band 6 continuum observations.

claims.hypothesis: Dust scale height differs between inner and outer rings of multi-ring disks
claims.experiment: Fit azimuthal intensity variations of two rings in each of six ALMA Band 6 disk images with a ring model via MCMC
claims.result: Inner ring H_d is 1.5-3.7 au (H_d/r 0.025-0.045) in four disks while outer rings have upper limits (<0.5-4.3 au); AS 209 and AA Tau give only upper limits for both rings
claims.finding: Inner rings are puffed up (comparable to gas scale height); outer rings are strongly settled

evidence.quote: inner rings exhibit puffed-up dust layers with heights comparable to the gas scale height, while outer rings are significantly more settled, with dust scale heights less than 20% of the gas scale height.
we found that, in 4 out of 6 disks, inner rings tend to exhibit puffed-up dust layers

claims.hypothesis: The settling efficiency alpha_z/St differs between inner and outer rings
claims.experiment: Compute alpha_z/St = (H_d/H_g)^2 using three gas-temperature estimates
claims.result: alpha_z/St ~0.1-0.5 in the four inner rings versus <0.04 in outer rings
claims.finding: Settling coefficient is at least an order of magnitude higher in inner rings

evidence.quote: the settling coefficient in the inner rings is at least one order of magnitude higher than the outer rings.

evidence.quote: This strongly favors scenario where enhanced turbulent diffusion in inner rings is larger than the outer ring by at least one magnitude.

Only six disks and two rings each, so the 4-of-6 occurrence rate has large small-number uncertainty; two disks (AS 209, AA Tau) give no constraint
Rings were selected as radially resolved and 'sharp', a selection that may favour particular ring types
